title: Song of Solomon Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Song of Solomon chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Song of Solomon Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Song of Solomon Chapter 6.

questions.question: Where has the beloved gone according to Song of Solomon 6:2?
options: To the beds of spices in his garden
questions.correctAnswer: To the beds of spices in his garden
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:2 states that the beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 6:3, what does the speaker declare about their relationship?
options: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine
My beloved is lost to me
I am searching for my beloved
questions.correctAnswer: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:3 clearly says, 'I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine.'

questions.question: How is the beloved described in Song of Solomon 6:4?
options: Beautiful as Tirzah and comely as Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Beautiful as Tirzah and comely as Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:4 describes the beloved as beautiful as Tirzah and comely as Jerusalem.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the beloved's hair in Song of Solomon 6:5?
options: As a flock of goats that appear from Gilead
As the waves of the sea
As the stars in the sky
questions.correctAnswer: As a flock of goats that appear from Gilead
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:5 compares the beloved's hair to a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 6:1 asks where the beloved has turned aside so they may seek him together.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:1 asks where the beloved has gone or turned aside so that they may seek him with the speaker.

questions.question: True or False: According to Song of Solomon 6:6, the beloved's teeth are compared to a flock of sheep bearing twins.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:6 says the teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, and each bears twins.

questions.question: True or False: The speaker in Song of Solomon 6:9 states that among many queens and concubines, her dove is the only one and undefiled.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:9 says, 'My dove, my undefiled is but one...the only one of her mother.'

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 6:7 compares the beloved's temples to a piece of a pomegranate within her locks.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:7 states, 'As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples within thy locks.'

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 6:8, how many queens are mentioned?
questions.correctAnswer: Sixty
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:8 says there are threescore (which means sixty) queens.

questions.question: Who is described as looking forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun in Song of Solomon 6:10?
questions.correctAnswer: The Shulamite
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:10 asks, 'Who is she that looketh forth as the morning...' referring to the Shulamite.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 6:11, where did the speaker go to see the fruits of the valley?
questions.correctAnswer: The garden of nuts
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:11 says the speaker went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley.

questions.question: What made the speaker's soul like the chariots of Amminadib in Song of Solomon 6:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Before the speaker was aware
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:12 states 'Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.'

questions.question: What is the repeated request made in Song of Solomon 6:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Return, return, O Shulamite
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:13 repeats the phrase 'Return, return, O Shulamite.'

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 6:5, what effect do the beloved's eyes have on the speaker?
questions.correctAnswer: They have overcome me
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:5 states, 'Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me.'

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 6, which event happens first?
options: The beloved goes down into his garden
The speaker describes the beloved's teeth
The speaker sees the fruits of the valley
The Shulamite is asked to return
questions.correctAnswer: The beloved goes down into his garden
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:2 states the beloved goes down into his garden before the later events.

medium.title: Song of Solomon Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Song of Solomon Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 6:6, what is compared to a flock of sheep which go up from the washing?
questions.correctAnswer: Thy teeth
questions.explanation: Verse 6 explicitly compares 'thy teeth' to 'a flock of sheep which go up from the washing.'

questions.question: What imagery is used in Song of Solomon 6:7 to describe the temples within her locks?
questions.correctAnswer: A piece of a pomegranate
questions.explanation: Verse 7 describes the temples within her locks as 'a piece of a pomegranate,' emphasizing beauty and intricacy.

questions.question: How many queens and concubines are mentioned in Song of Solomon 6:8?
options: A hundred queens and two hundred concubines
questions.correctAnswer: Threescore queens and fourscore concubines
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states there are 'threescore queens, and fourscore concubines,' highlighting the multitude.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 6:9, who is praised above all the queens and concubines?
questions.correctAnswer: My dove, my undefiled
questions.explanation: Verse 9 emphasizes that 'My dove, my undefiled is but one,' and she is praised above all others.

questions.question: How does Song of Solomon 6:10 describe the woman who looks forth as the morning?
options: Fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners
Beautiful as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem
Like a garden of spices and lilies
As a flock of sheep going up from washing
questions.correctAnswer: Fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners
questions.explanation: Verse 10 uses this imagery to depict the woman's radiant and powerful appearance.

questions.question: What does Song of Solomon 6:11 say the speaker went down into the garden of nuts to see?
options: The fruits of the valley and whether the vine flourished
questions.correctAnswer: The fruits of the valley and whether the vine flourished
questions.explanation: Verse 11 explicitly states the speaker went to observe the fruits and the flourishing vine.

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 6:12, what does the soul make the speaker like?
questions.correctAnswer: The chariots of Amminadib
questions.explanation: Verse 12 compares the soul's stirring to the swift chariots of Amminadib.

questions.question: What is the repeated exhortation in Song of Solomon 6:13 directed to the Shulamite?
options: Return, return, that we may look upon thee
questions.correctAnswer: Return, return, that we may look upon thee
questions.explanation: Verse 13 repeats 'Return, return' as a call to the Shulamite to come back and be seen.

questions.question: What does Song of Solomon 6:9 teach about uniqueness and value in Christian living?
options: Being chosen and undefiled is precious and worthy of praise
Having many companions is the greatest blessing
Power is shown by the number of queens and concubines
Beauty is only external and fleeting
questions.correctAnswer: Being chosen and undefiled is precious and worthy of praise
questions.explanation: Verse 9 highlights the value of being 'my dove, my undefiled' and chosen, teaching the importance of purity and being cherished.

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 6:6 says that none of the teeth are barren.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states, 'there is not one barren among them,' referring to the teeth.

questions.question: True or False: According to Song of Solomon 6:8, there are exactly one hundred queens.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 8 lists 'threescore queens,' which is sixty, not one hundred.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 6:7 and 6:8, what two images together emphasize the beauty and multitude surrounding the beloved?
options: Temples like pomegranate pieces and threescore queens with fourscore concubines
Flocks of sheep and lilies in the garden
Chariots of Amminadib and an army with banners
questions.correctAnswer: Temples like pomegranate pieces and threescore queens with fourscore concubines
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 together use the imagery of pomegranate temples and many queens and concubines to highlight beauty and greatness.

questions.question: How does Song of Solomon 6:9-10 deepen the understanding of the beloved's uniqueness and radiance?
options: By describing her as the only undefiled one and likening her to the morning, moon, and sun
By comparing her to many queens and concubines
By stating she is terrible as an army with banners only
By emphasizing her hair like a flock of goats
questions.correctAnswer: By describing her as the only undefiled one and likening her to the morning, moon, and sun
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 highlight her singular purity and radiant beauty with celestial imagery.

questions.question: What spiritual lesson can be drawn from the invitation in Song of Solomon 6:13 to the Shulamite to return that they may look upon her?
options: Believers are encouraged to come back to fellowship and be seen by the community
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are encouraged to come back to fellowship and be seen by the community
questions.explanation: Verse 13 invites the Shulamite to return so others may look upon her, teaching the value of returning to fellowship and being part of the community.

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 6:5 says the beloved's hair is compared to a flock of sheep.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 5 compares the hair to a flock of goats, not sheep; the teeth are compared to sheep in verse 6.

hard.title: Song of Solomon Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Song of Solomon Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 6:11, what is the speaker going down into the garden of nuts to observe?
options: The fruits of the valley and whether the vine flourished and the pomegranates budded
The lilies and spices in the garden
The flock of sheep ascending from washing
questions.correctAnswer: The fruits of the valley and whether the vine flourished and the pomegranates budded
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:11 explicitly states that the speaker goes down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley and to see whether the vine flourished and the pomegranates budded.

questions.question: What simile is used in Song of Solomon 6:12 to describe the speaker's soul?
options: As a piece of a pomegranate
questions.correctAnswer: Like the chariots of Amminadib
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:12 compares the speaker's soul to the chariots of Amminadib, indicating swift and powerful movement.

questions.question: What is the significance of the term 'Shulamite' in the context of Song of Solomon 6:13?
options: It refers to a woman of Shunem, symbolizing beauty and beloved status
It is a name for the beloved’s garden
It describes a type of pomegranate
It is an ancient army mentioned in the text
questions.correctAnswer: It refers to a woman of Shunem, symbolizing beauty and beloved status
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:13 calls the beloved the 'Shulamite,' a term traditionally understood to mean a woman from Shunem, symbolizing her unique beauty and beloved status.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a similar theme of beloved and garden imagery as seen in Song of Solomon 6:11-13?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 2:8-9
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:8-9 describes the Garden of Eden with trees and fruits, paralleling the garden imagery in Song of Solomon 6:11-13 where the beloved is associated with flourishing gardens and fruits.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Song of Solomon 6:13 with the repeated phrase 'Return, return'?
questions.correctAnswer: Repetition for emphasis
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Return, return' in Song of Solomon 6:13 uses repetition to emphasize the invitation to the Shulamite to come back and be seen, highlighting the importance of her presence.

questions.question: How does the description of the Shulamite in Song of Solomon 6:13 relate to military imagery?
options: She is compared to the company of two armies, indicating strength and majesty
She wears armor like a soldier
She leads an army in battle
She is described as a fortress
questions.correctAnswer: She is compared to the company of two armies, indicating strength and majesty
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:13 describes the Shulamite as resembling the company of two armies, a metaphor for her formidable and majestic presence.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 6:9, how is the beloved described among queens, concubines, and virgins?
options: She is the only one of her mother, the choice one, and praised by all
She is one among many and indistinguishable
She is less favored than the concubines
She is not mentioned among them
questions.correctAnswer: She is the only one of her mother, the choice one, and praised by all
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:9 states that the beloved is the only one of her mother, the choice one, and receives blessings and praise from daughters, queens, and concubines alike.

questions.question: True or False: The reference to 'chariots of Amminadib' in Song of Solomon 6:12 symbolizes swift movement and excitement.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:12 uses the imagery of 'chariots of Amminadib' to express the soul's swift and eager motion, symbolizing excitement and urgency.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew term 'Shulamite' as it applies in Song of Solomon 6:13?
options: Peaceful or perfect woman from Shunem
questions.correctAnswer: Peaceful or perfect woman from Shunem
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Shulamite' likely derives from Shunem and connotes 'peaceful' or 'perfect,' denoting the beloved woman’s origin and ideal character as seen in Song of Solomon 6:13.

questions.question: How does Song of Solomon 6:4's comparison of the beloved to Tirzah and Jerusalem relate to the theme of beauty and strength?
options: It juxtaposes physical beauty with formidable power
It only praises her physical beauty
It suggests she is a conquered city
questions.correctAnswer: It juxtaposes physical beauty with formidable power
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:4 compares the beloved’s beauty to Tirzah and Jerusalem, cities known for their splendor and strength, highlighting both her attractiveness and commanding presence.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of mutual belonging found in Song of Solomon 6:3 ('I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine')?
questions.correctAnswer: John 15:9
questions.explanation: John 15:9 speaks of abiding in love mutually as Jesus and the Father abide in each other, resonating with the mutual belonging expressed in Song of Solomon 6:3.

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 6:6, the beloved’s teeth are compared to what agricultural imagery?
options: A flock of sheep which go up from the washing, each bearing twins, with none barren
A cluster of grapes in the vineyard
questions.correctAnswer: A flock of sheep which go up from the washing, each bearing twins, with none barren
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:6 likens the beloved’s teeth to a flock of sheep recently washed, each bearing twins and none barren, symbolizing purity and completeness.

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 6:8 suggests that there are more queens than concubines.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:8 states there are threescore (60) queens and fourscore (80) concubines, meaning there are more concubines than queens.

questions.question: How does Song of Solomon 6:7's imagery of the beloved's temples like a piece of pomegranate function as a literary device?
options: It is a metaphor highlighting beauty and delicacy
It is an example of hyperbole
It is a direct historical reference
It uses irony to contrast appearance
questions.correctAnswer: It is a metaphor highlighting beauty and delicacy
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:7 uses metaphor comparing the beloved’s temples to a piece of pomegranate, emphasizing the beauty and delicacy of her features.

questions.question: Which cultural significance does the 'garden of nuts' in Song of Solomon 6:11 reflect in the ancient Near Eastern context?
options: A symbol of fertility and abundance
A place of exile and desolation
questions.correctAnswer: A symbol of fertility and abundance
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, gardens, including those with nuts, symbolized fertility and abundance, aligning with the imagery in Song of Solomon 6:11 where the garden represents flourishing life.

theological.title: Song of Solomon Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Song of Solomon Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 6:3, what mutual possession is expressed between the lovers?
options: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine
I am alone in the garden
My beloved is a mighty warrior
questions.correctAnswer: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:3 states the mutual belonging between the lovers, emphasizing their reciprocal love and union.

questions.question: What simile does the bride use in Song of Solomon 6:5 to describe her beloved’s hair?
options: As a flock of goats that appear from Gilead
As golden wheat in the field
As the waves of the sea
As the stars in the sky
questions.correctAnswer: As a flock of goats that appear from Gilead
questions.explanation: In Song of Solomon 6:5, the beloved’s hair is poetically compared to a flock of goats appearing from Gilead, symbolizing beauty and abundance.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about the beloved’s purity is conveyed in Song of Solomon 6:9?
options: My dove, my undefiled is but one
She is a common figure among many
questions.correctAnswer: My dove, my undefiled is but one
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:9 teaches the uniqueness and purity of the beloved, highlighting the doctrine of sanctification and being set apart as undefiled.

questions.question: How does Song of Solomon 6:4 describe the beloved’s beauty with a comparison to cities and armies?
options: As beautiful as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners
As strong as Babylon, mighty as Egypt
As radiant as the sun, gentle as a lamb
As hidden as a secret garden
questions.correctAnswer: As beautiful as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:4 uses the imagery of Tirzah and Jerusalem combined with the terror of an army with banners to express the beloved’s majestic and awe-inspiring beauty.

questions.question: What does the phrase "to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies" in Song of Solomon 6:2 symbolize in a Christological sense?
options: Christ’s nurturing and gathering of His church
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s nurturing and gathering of His church
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:2 symbolizes Christ’s pastoral care and His gathering of believers, reflecting His role as the Good Shepherd (John 10:11) who nurtures His flock.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by the description of the beloved as 'terrible as an army with banners' in Song of Solomon 6:4?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s majesty and power
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:4’s depiction of the beloved as 'terrible as an army with banners' reveals God’s majestic and powerful nature, highlighting His awe-inspiring presence (Exodus 15:6).

questions.question: Based on Song of Solomon 6:6, what theological significance might the metaphor of 'thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing' hold?
options: It symbolizes purity and fruitfulness in sanctification
It refers to physical strength alone
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes purity and fruitfulness in sanctification
questions.explanation: The metaphor in Song of Solomon 6:6 signifies purity and fruitfulness, reflecting the doctrine of sanctification where believers are cleansed and bear spiritual fruit (John 15:5).

questions.question: How does Song of Solomon 6:13 contribute to the narrative arc of the bride’s identity in the redemptive story?
options: It calls for the Shulamite’s return, emphasizing restoration and witness
It speaks of her earthly exile
questions.correctAnswer: It calls for the Shulamite’s return, emphasizing restoration and witness
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:13’s invitation for the Shulamite to return symbolizes restoration and the believer’s call to be a faithful witness in the redemptive narrative (Isaiah 62:6-7).

questions.question: What combined theological insight can be drawn from Song of Solomon 6:8-9 regarding the uniqueness of the beloved?
options: Despite many queens and concubines, the beloved is uniquely chosen and undefiled
The beloved is one among many equals
The beloved is rejected by others
The beloved is common and unremarkable
questions.correctAnswer: Despite many queens and concubines, the beloved is uniquely chosen and undefiled
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 highlight the beloved’s singularity and purity amid numerous others, illustrating the doctrine of election and sanctification within the church (Ephesians 1:4).

questions.question: What does the phrase "my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib" in Song of Solomon 6:12 metaphorically express about the believer’s experience?
options: A rapid, Spirit-driven movement toward God
questions.correctAnswer: A rapid, Spirit-driven movement toward God
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:12 metaphorically expresses the believer’s swift, Spirit-empowered zeal to pursue God, akin to chariots symbolizing strength and speed (2 Samuel 2:14).

questions.question: Sceptics claim Song of Solomon is merely secular love poetry with no spiritual significance. What does Song of Solomon 6:1-3 actually teach about the nature of divine love?
options: It depicts a profound mutual belonging that models Christ and the Church’s love
It only describes human romantic love
It is unrelated to divine themes
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts a profound mutual belonging that models Christ and the Church’s love
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:1-3 reveals the mutual possession and intimate union that allegorically models Christ’s love for His Church (Ephesians 5:25-27), countering secular-only interpretations.

questions.question: What narrative arc does Song of Solomon 6:11 reflect in the broader redemptive story?
options: The believer’s examination of spiritual fruitfulness and flourishing
questions.correctAnswer: The believer’s examination of spiritual fruitfulness and flourishing
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:11 depicts the search for flourishing fruit, which typifies the believer’s self-examination and growth in sanctification within the redemptive narrative (Galatians 5:22-23).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly reflected in the exclusivity of the beloved described in Song of Solomon 6:9?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness in election
questions.explanation: The exclusivity of the beloved in Song of Solomon 6:9 reflects the doctrine of God’s faithful election, emphasizing His sovereign choosing of His people (Romans 8:30).

questions.question: Combining Song of Solomon 6:5 and 6:7, what theological insight emerges about the beloved’s physical and spiritual beauty?
options: Her physical features symbolize both natural beauty and inner sanctity
questions.correctAnswer: Her physical features symbolize both natural beauty and inner sanctity
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 7 use imagery of hair and temples to show that the beloved’s beauty encompasses both external and internal holiness, reflecting sanctification (Psalm 45:11).

questions.question: What doctrine is highlighted by the repeated call to 'return' in Song of Solomon 6:13?
options: The doctrine of repentance and restoration
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of repentance and restoration
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 6:13’s repeated call to return emphasizes repentance and restoration, central to salvation and sanctification (Joel 2:12-13).
